A018.why: Confirmed. I could not break it, and no call sequence can. The mutant changes storeSequencerSetVerifyHash from mstore(add(P,185),0) to mstore(add(P,186),0). Compiled, Rollup differs by exactly one byte: PUSH1 0xb9 becomes 0xba, at runtime offset 22899 with the optimizer off and 20812 with it on (999999 runs); the creation code also differs by one byte. The only call site is Rollup.sol:351 in _commitBatchWithBatchData, always with bytes32(0). In both builds it is followed directly by storeParentBatchHash's mstore at P+217, where P is the header pointer, i.e. the free pointer after _commitBatch. So after line 352 memory is identical in both, except that the mutant leaves byte P+185 untouched instead of zeroing it. P+185 is never written earlier in the call frame: (1) The proxy's delegatecall gives Rollup fresh memory, and the free pointer only grows. (2) The only writes that can land above the pointer before the header build are the external-call argument encodings and _commitBatch's prefix. isActive(address) and getCrossDomainMessage(uint256) write 36 bytes, getFirstUnfinalizedMessageEnqueueTime() writes 32. Each call is followed by a pointer bump of roundup(returndatasize), which is at least 32 because a shorter reply reverts in decoding; so at most 4 bytes stay above the pointer. _commitBatch's two mstores reach F+40 while the pointer moves to F+10+32n. (3) Everything else stays below the pointer: the parent-header calldatacopy writes exactly length bytes and bumps by length; the V2 blob loop bumps by 32k; mapping keccaks use scratch space 0x00-0x3f. Nothing on the success path before the build emits an event, abi-encodes or builds a revert string. Hence the only memory above P is [P,P+30) of zeros when n=0, or [P,P+4) holding the low bytes of the last L1 message index when n>=1. So the header bytes, the keccak batch hash, the CommitBatch event and every storage slot are equal. That holds for commitBatch, commitState and commitBatchWithProof; for new and parent versions 0/1/2, including V0 parents of any length >= 249; and for any callee return length, msg.sender or message index. Gas: the opcode is the same, and memory size after the parent-hash store is the same, so cumulative gas there is equal. An out-of-gas between the two stores in one build forces an out-of-gas by the parent store in the other, giving the same halt; no gas limit distinguishes them. A051.why: Confirmed. In both mutants the challengeState loop runs zero iterations in every state. A050 starts at lastCommitted+1 and continues while i <= lastCommitted. A051 starts at lastFinalized+1 and continues while i <= lastFinalized. Neither checked '+1' can overflow, because indices stay at or below 2^64 (the batch index is a 64-bit header field). The loop body never runs, and everything else is identical source, so every observable matches A050. Evidence, comparing A050 with A051 directly: 40 targeted scenarios, including challenges with lastCommitted - lastFinalized from 0 to 5, and 550 random sequences, including 158 successful challenges with lastCommitted >= lastFinalized+2. No difference. The same harness distinguishes the original from A050 on 15 of 60 seeds.

A042.why:
Could not break it.

When initialize2 can run: it is reinitializer(2), so only while _initialized is 0 or 1. Any of initialize2, initialize3 or initialize4 closes it for good, and nothing lowers _initialized.

Before importGenesisBatch: no commit, revert or finalize can pass. Each needs committedBatches[i] == keccak(header), and every entry is 0. So lastCommitted == lastFinalized == 0, and both versions read the same slot.

After genesis: importGenesisBatch runs only once, because finalizedStateRoots[0] becomes non-zero and index 0 is never written again. Three invariants then hold:
(I1) committedBatches[j] != 0 iff j <= lastCommitted. A commit writes only lastCommitted+1, finalize never touches committedBatches, and revertBatch must zero through the top: it requires committedBatches[b+count] == 0 and loops to the first zero.
(I2) lastFinalized <= lastCommitted. finalizeBatch(i) needs batch i committed, and revert sets b-1 with b > lastFinalized.
(I3) committedStateRoots[j] != 0 for every j in [lastFinalized, lastCommitted]. Each commit writes a required-non-zero postStateRoot at the new top, and revert touches no roots.
